challenges.name: scope-functions-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: let, apply, also and ?: run
challenges.description: Trace a ?.let { } ?: fallback whose lambda returns null, then pick the scope-function and extension statements that are true.

questions.question:
sendPush returns an error message, or null when the push was sent. What does this print?

fun sendPush(token: String, text: String): String? {
    println("push")
    return null
}

val token: String? = "tok-1"
token?.let { sendPush(it, "Order on its way") } ?: println("sms")
questions.explanation: token is not null, so let runs the lambda: sendPush prints push and returns null. let returns whatever its lambda returns, so the whole expression token?.let { ... } is null, and the elvis operator runs its right side: sms is printed too. The elvis does not know WHY the left side is null: a null token and a lambda that returned null look the same. That is how customers received a push and an SMS for the same order. An if (token != null) ... else ... has no such ambiguity.

options.text: Nothing: sendPush returned null, so nothing was sent

questions.question: Which of these statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: apply runs the block with the object as this and returns the object itself, so n is the configured Notification. let returns the lambda's result: "cho xanh".let { it.uppercase() } is "CHO XANH". also passes the object as it and returns the object, so the list (now [1, 2], because += changed it inside the block) is assigned to y. "abc".also { it.length } returns "abc", not 3: also ignores the lambda's result. An extension function is resolved statically and only sees the public API of its receiver; it cannot read private members. An extension on a nullable receiver (String?) can be called on a null value: inside it, this is null, so s.orDash() returns "-".

options.text: val n = Notification().apply { title = "Hi" } makes n the Notification object
val x = "cho xanh".let { it.uppercase() } makes x "CHO XANH"
val y = mutableListOf(1).also { it += 2 } makes y [1, 2]
An extension function on a class can read that class's private properties
With fun String?.orDash() = this ?: "-" and val s: String? = null, s.orDash() returns "-"

challenges.name: notification-extensions
challenges.title: Write the notification text with extension functions
challenges.description: The Cho Xanh 'order on its way' notification needs money with thousands separators, names in title case, a masked driver phone number and a dash for missing values. Write the extension functions Long.vnd(), String.titleCase(), String.maskPhone() and String?.orDash(), then build Order.notificationText() from them. Negative amounts (refunds), short phone numbers, extra spaces in names and notes that are only spaces must all come out right. The test runner reads order and refund lines and prints one text per line.

tests.name: A complete order
tests.input: order|CX-1042|nguyen van an|1250000|tuan|0912345678|leave at the door
tests.expected: Hi Nguyen Van An, order CX-1042 (1,250,000 VND) is on its way. Driver: Tuan (091****678). Note: leave at the door

tests.name: No driver yet and no note
tests.expected: Hi Le Thi Mai, order CX-1043 (245,000 VND) is on its way. Driver: - (-). Note: -

tests.name: Refunds and a small amount
tests.expected:
Refund for CX-1042: -300,000 VND
Refund for CX-1044: -30,000 VND
Hi Minh, order CX-1045 (999 VND) is on its way. Driver: Lan (098****321). Note: -

tests.name: Messy names and a note of only spaces
tests.input: order|CX-1046|  TRAN   thi   HA |85000|  pham  QUANG |0987654321|
tests.expected: Hi Tran Thi Ha, order CX-1046 (85,000 VND) is on its way. Driver: Pham Quang (098****321). Note: -

tests.name: A short phone number and zero amounts

Hi Binh, order CX-1047 (0 VND) is on its way. Driver: Son (*****). Note: ring twice
